ESV.1: Now Joseph had been brought down to Egypt, and Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, the captain of the guard, an Egyptian, had bought him from the Ishmaelites who had brought him down there.
ESV.2: The LORD was with Joseph, and he became a successful man, and he was in the house of his Egyptian master.
ESV.3: His master saw that the LORD was with him and that the LORD caused all that he did to succeed in his hands.
ESV.4: So Joseph found favor in his sight and attended him, and he made him overseer of his house and put him in charge of all that he had.
ESV.5: From the time that he made him overseer in his house and over all that he had, the LORD blessed the Egyptian's house for Joseph's sake; the blessing of the LORD was on all that he had, in house and field.
ESV.6: So he left all that he had in Joseph's charge, and because of him he had no concern about anything but the food he ate. Now Joseph was handsome in form and appearance.
ESV.7: And after a time his master's wife cast her eyes on Joseph and said, “Lie with me.”
ESV.8: But he refused and said to his master's wife, “Behold, because of me my master has no concern about anything in the house, and he has put everything that he has in my charge.
ESV.9: He is not greater in this house than I am, nor has he kept back anything from me except you, because you are his wife. How then can I do this great wickedness and sin against God?”
ESV.10: And as she spoke to Joseph day after day, he would not listen to her, to lie beside her or to be with her.
ESV.11: But one day, when he went into the house to do his work and none of the men of the house was there in the house,
ESV.12: she caught him by his garment, saying, “Lie with me.” But he left his garment in her hand and fled and got out of the house.
ESV.13: And as soon as she saw that he had left his garment in her hand and had fled out of the house,
ESV.14: she called to the men of her household and said to them, “See, he has brought among us a Hebrew to laugh at us. He came in to me to lie with me, and I cried out with a loud voice.
ESV.15: And as soon as he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried out, he left his garment beside me and fled and got out of the house.”
ESV.16: Then she laid up his garment by her until his master came home,
ESV.17: and she told him the same story, saying, “The Hebrew servant, whom you have brought among us, came in to me to laugh at me.
ESV.18: But as soon as I lifted up my voice and cried, he left his garment beside me and fled out of the house.”
ESV.19: As soon as his master heard the words that his wife spoke to him, “This is the way your servant treated me,” his anger was kindled.
ESV.20: And Joseph's master took him and put him into the prison, the place where the king's prisoners were confined, and he was there in prison.
ESV.21: But the LORD was with Joseph and showed him steadfast love and gave him favor in the sight of the keeper of the prison.
ESV.22: And the keeper of the prison put Joseph in charge of all the prisoners who were in the prison. Whatever was done there, he was the one who did it.
ESV.23: The keeper of the prison paid no attention to anything that was in Joseph's charge, because the LORD was with him. And whatever he did, the LORD made it succeed.

NASB.1: Now Joseph had been taken down to Egypt; and Potiphar, an Egyptian officer of Pharaoh, the captain of the bodyguard, bought him from the Ishmaelites, who had taken him down there.
NASB.2: The LORD was with Joseph, so he became a successful man. And he was in the house of his master, the Egyptian.
NASB.3: Now his master saw that the LORD was with him and [how] the LORD caused all that he did to prosper in his hand.
NASB.4: So Joseph found favor in his sight and became his personal servant; and he made him overseer over his house, and all that he owned he put in his charge.
NASB.5: It came about that from the time he made him overseer in his house and over all that he owned, the LORD blessed the Egyptian's house on account of Joseph; thus the LORD'S blessing was upon all that he owned, in the house and in the field.
NASB.6: So he left everything he owned in Joseph's charge; and with him [there] he did not concern himself with anything except the food which he ate. Now Joseph was handsome in form and appearance.
NASB.7: It came about after these events that his master's wife looked with desire at Joseph, and she said, 'Lie with me.'
NASB.8: But he refused and said to his master's wife, 'Behold, with me [here], my master does not concern himself with anything in the house, and he has put all that he owns in my charge.
NASB.9: 'There is no one greater in this house than I, and he has withheld nothing from me except you, because you are his wife. How then could I do this great evil and sin against God?'
NASB.10: As she spoke to Joseph day after day, he did not listen to her to lie beside her [or] be with her.
NASB.11: Now it happened one day that he went into the house to do his work, and none of the men of the household was there inside.
NASB.12: She caught him by his garment, saying, 'Lie with me!' And he left his garment in her hand and fled, and went outside.
NASB.13: When she saw that he had left his garment in her hand and had fled outside,
NASB.14: she called to the men of her household and said to them, 'See, he has brought in a Hebrew to us to make sport of us; he came in to me to lie with me, and I screamed.
NASB.15: 'When he heard that I raised my voice and screamed, he left his garment beside me and fled and went outside.'
NASB.16: So she left his garment beside her until his master came home.
NASB.17: Then she spoke to him with these words, 'The Hebrew slave, whom you brought to us, came in to me to make sport of me;
NASB.18: and as I raised my voice and screamed, he left his garment beside me and fled outside.'
NASB.19: Now when his master heard the words of his wife, which she spoke to him, saying, 'This is what your slave did to me,' his anger burned.
NASB.20: So Joseph's master took him and put him into the jail, the place where the king's prisoners were confined; and he was there in the jail.
NASB.21: But the LORD was with Joseph and extended kindness to him, and gave him favor in the sight of the chief jailer.
NASB.22: The chief jailer committed to Joseph's charge all the prisoners who were in the jail; so that whatever was done there, he was responsible [for it].
NASB.23: The chief jailer did not supervise anything under Joseph's charge because the LORD was with him; and whatever he did, the LORD made to prosper.

NKJV.1: Now Joseph had been taken down to Egypt. And Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh, captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him from the Ishmaelites who had taken him down there.
NKJV.2: The LORD was with Joseph, and he was a successful man; and he was in the house of his master the Egyptian.
NKJV.3: And his master saw that the LORD was with him and that the LORD made all he did to prosper in his hand.
NKJV.4: So Joseph found favor in his sight, and served him. Then he made him overseer of his house, and all that he had he put under his authority.
NKJV.5: So it was, from the time that he had made him overseer of his house and all that he had, that the LORD blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake; and the blessing of the LORD was on all that he had in the house and in the field.
NKJV.6: Thus he left all that he had in Joseph’s hand, and he did not know what he had except for the bread which he ate. Now Joseph was handsome in form and appearance.
NKJV.7: And it came to pass after these things that his master’s wife cast longing eyes on Joseph, and she said, “Lie with me.”
NKJV.8: But he refused and said to his master’s wife, “Look, my master does not know what is with me in the house, and he has committed all that he has to my hand.
NKJV.9: There is no one greater in this house than I, nor has he kept back anything from me but you, because you are his wife. How then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?”
NKJV.10: So it was, as she spoke to Joseph day by day, that he did not heed her, to lie with her or to be with her.
NKJV.11: But it happened about this time, when Joseph went into the house to do his work, and none of the men of the house was inside,
NKJV.12: that she caught him by his garment, saying, “Lie with me.” But he left his garment in her hand, and fled and ran outside.
NKJV.13: And so it was, when she saw that he had left his garment in her hand and fled outside,
NKJV.14: that she called to the men of her house and spoke to them, saying, “See, he has brought in to us a Hebrew to mock us. He came in to me to lie with me, and I cried out with a loud voice.
NKJV.15: And it happened, when he heard that I lifted my voice and cried out, that he left his garment with me, and fled and went outside.”
NKJV.16: So she kept his garment with her until his master came home.
NKJV.17: Then she spoke to him with words like these, saying, “The Hebrew servant whom you brought to us came in to me to mock me;
NKJV.18: so it happened, as I lifted my voice and cried out, that he left his garment with me and fled outside.”
NKJV.19: So it was, when his master heard the words which his wife spoke to him, saying, “Your servant did to me after this manner,” that his anger was aroused.
NKJV.20: Then Joseph’s master took him and put him into the prison, a place where the king’s prisoners were confined. And he was there in the prison.
NKJV.21: But the LORD was with Joseph and showed him mercy, and He gave him favor in the sight of the keeper of the prison.
NKJV.22: And the keeper of the prison committed to Joseph’s hand all the prisoners who were in the prison; whatever they did there, it was his doing.
NKJV.23: The keeper of the prison did not look into anything that was under Joseph’s authority, because the LORD was with him; and whatever he did, the LORD made it prosper.

WEB.16: She laid up his garment by her, until his master came home.

WEB.18: and as I lifted up my voice and cried, he left his garment by me, and ran outside.”

WEB.21: But Yahweh was with Joseph, and showed kindness to him, and gave him favor in the sight of the keeper of the prison.

CSB17.1: Now Joseph had been taken to Egypt. An Egyptian named Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh and the captain of the guards, bought him from the Ishmaelites <sup>ⓚ</sup> who had brought him there.
CSB17.2: The LORD was with Joseph, <sup>ⓛ</sup> and he became a successful man, serving <sup>[1]</sup> in the household of his Egyptian master.
CSB17.3: When his master saw that the LORD was with him and that the LORD made everything he did successful, <sup>ⓜ</sup>
CSB17.4: Joseph found favor <sup>ⓝ</sup> with his master and became his personal attendant. Potiphar also put him in charge of his household and placed all that he owned under his authority. <sup>[2]</sup>
CSB17.5: From the time that he put him in charge of his household and of all that he owned, the LORD blessed the Egyptian’s house because of Joseph. <sup>ⓐ</sup> The LORD’s blessing was on all that he owned, in his house and in his fields.
CSB17.6: He left all that he owned under Joseph’s authority; <sup>[3]</sup> he did not concern himself with anything except the food he ate. Now Joseph was well-built and handsome. <sup>ⓑ</sup>
CSB17.7: After some time <sup>[4]</sup> his master’s wife looked longingly at Joseph and said, “Sleep with me.”
CSB17.8: But he refused. “Look,” he said to his master’s wife, “with me here my master does not concern himself with anything in his house, and he has put all that he owns under my authority. <sup>[5]</sup>
CSB17.9: No one in this house is greater than I am. He has withheld nothing from me except you, because you are his wife. So how could I do this immense evil, and how could I sin against God?” <sup>ⓒ</sup>
CSB17.10: Although she spoke to Joseph day after day, he refused to go to bed with her. <sup>[6]</sup>
CSB17.11: Now one day he went into the house to do his work, and none of the household servants were there. <sup>[7]</sup>
CSB17.12: She grabbed him by his garment and said, “Sleep with me!” But leaving his garment in her hand, he escaped and ran outside.
CSB17.13: When she saw that he had left his garment with her and had run outside,
CSB17.14: she called her household servants. “Look,” she said to them, “my husband brought a Hebrew man to make fools of us. He came to me so he could sleep with me, and I screamed as loud as I could.
CSB17.15: When he heard me screaming for help, <sup>[8]</sup> he left his garment beside me and ran outside.”
CSB17.16: She put Joseph’s garment beside her until his master came home.
CSB17.17: Then she told him the same story: “The Hebrew slave you brought to us came to make a fool of me,
CSB17.18: but when I screamed for help, <sup>[9]</sup> he left his garment beside me and ran outside.”
CSB17.19: When his master heard the story his wife told him — “These are the things your slave did to me” — he was furious
CSB17.20: and had him thrown into prison, <sup>ⓓ</sup> where the king’s prisoners were confined. So Joseph was there in prison.
CSB17.21: But the LORD was with Joseph and extended kindness to him. <sup>ⓔ</sup> He granted him favor with the prison warden. <sup>ⓕ</sup>
CSB17.22: The warden put all the prisoners who were in the prison under Joseph’s authority, <sup>[10]</sup> and he was responsible for everything that was done there.
CSB17.23: The warden did not bother with anything under Joseph’s authority, <sup>[11]</sup> because the LORD was with him, and the LORD made everything that he did successful. <sup>ⓖ</sup>

NLT.1: When Joseph was taken to Egypt by the Ishmaelite traders, he was purchased by Potiphar, an Egyptian officer. Potiphar was captain of the guard for Pharaoh, the king of Egypt.
NLT.2: The LORD was with Joseph, so he succeeded in everything he did as he served in the home of his Egyptian master.
NLT.3: Potiphar noticed this and realized that the LORD was with Joseph, giving him success in everything he did.
NLT.4: This pleased Potiphar, so he soon made Joseph his personal attendant. He put him in charge of his entire household and everything he owned.
NLT.5: From the day Joseph was put in charge of his master’s household and property, the LORD began to bless Potiphar’s household for Joseph’s sake. All his household affairs ran smoothly, and his crops and livestock flourished.
NLT.6: So Potiphar gave Joseph complete administrative responsibility over everything he owned. With Joseph there, he didn’t worry about a thing — except what kind of food to eat! Joseph was a very handsome and well-built young man,
NLT.7: and Potiphar’s wife soon began to look at him lustfully. “Come and sleep with me,” she demanded.
NLT.8: But Joseph refused. “Look,” he told her, “my master trusts me with everything in his entire household.
NLT.9: No one here has more authority than I do. He has held back nothing from me except you, because you are his wife. How could I do such a wicked thing? It would be a great sin against God.”
NLT.10: She kept putting pressure on Joseph day after day, but he refused to sleep with her, and he kept out of her way as much as possible.
NLT.11: One day, however, no one else was around when he went in to do his work.
NLT.12: She came and grabbed him by his cloak, demanding, “Come on, sleep with me!” Joseph tore himself away, but he left his cloak in her hand as he ran from the house.
NLT.13: When she saw that she was holding his cloak and he had fled,
NLT.14: she called out to her servants. Soon all the men came running. “Look!” she said. “My husband has brought this Hebrew slave here to make fools of us! He came into my room to rape me, but I screamed.
NLT.15: When he heard me scream, he ran outside and got away, but he left his cloak behind with me.”
NLT.16: She kept the cloak with her until her husband came home.
NLT.17: Then she told him her story. “That Hebrew slave you’ve brought into our house tried to come in and fool around with me,” she said.
NLT.18: “But when I screamed, he ran outside, leaving his cloak with me!”
NLT.19: Potiphar was furious when he heard his wife’s story about how Joseph had treated her.
NLT.20: So he took Joseph and threw him into the prison where the king’s prisoners were held, and there he remained.
NLT.21: But the LORD was with Joseph in the prison and showed him his faithful love. And the LORD made Joseph a favorite with the prison warden.
NLT.22: Before long, the warden put Joseph in charge of all the other prisoners and over everything that happened in the prison.
NLT.23: The warden had no more worries, because Joseph took care of everything. The LORD was with him and caused everything he did to succeed.

AMP.1: Now Joseph had been taken down to Egypt; and Potiphar, an Egyptian officer of Pharaoh, the captain of the [royal] guard, bought him from the Ishmaelites, who had taken him down there.
AMP.2: The LORD was with Joseph, and he [even though a slave] became a successful and prosperous man; and he was in the house of his master, the Egyptian.
AMP.3: Now his master saw that the LORD was with him and that the LORD caused all that he did to prosper (succeed) in his hand.
AMP.4: So Joseph pleased Potiphar and found favor in his sight and he served him as his personal servant. He made Joseph overseer over his house, and he put all that he owned in Joseph's charge.
AMP.5: It happened that from the time that he made Joseph overseer in his house and [put him in charge] over all that he owned, that the LORD blessed the Egyptian's house because of Joseph; so the Lord's blessing was on everything that Potiphar owned, in the house and in the field.
AMP.6:
So Potiphar left all that he owned in Joseph's charge; and with Joseph there he did not [need to] pay attention to anything except the food he ate.
Now Joseph was handsome and attractive in form and appearance.
AMP.7: Then after a time his master's wife looked at Joseph with desire, and she said, "Lie with me."
AMP.8: But he refused and said to his master's wife, "Look, with me in the house, my master does not concern himself with anything; he has put everything that he owns in my charge.
AMP.9: He is not greater in this house than I am, nor has he kept anything from me except you, because you are his wife. How then could I do this great evil and sin against God [and your husband]?"
AMP.10: And so it was that she spoke to Joseph [persistently] day after day, but he did not listen to her [plea] to lie beside her or be with her.
AMP.11: Then it happened one day that Joseph went into the house to attend to his duties, and none of the men of the household was there in the house.
AMP.12: She caught Joseph by his [outer] robe, saying, "Lie with me!" But he left his robe in her hand and ran, and got outside [the house].
AMP.13: When she saw that he had left his robe in her hand and had run outside,
AMP.14: she called to the men of her household and said to them, "Look at this, your master has brought a Hebrew [into the household] to mock and insult us; he came to me to lie with me, and I screamed.
AMP.15: When he heard me screaming, he left his robe with me and ran outside [the house]."
AMP.16: So she left Joseph's [outer] robe beside her until his master came home.
AMP.17: Then she told her husband the same story, saying, "The Hebrew servant, whom you brought among us, came to me to mock and insult me;
AMP.18: then as soon as I raised my voice and screamed, he left his robe with me and ran outside [the house]."
AMP.19: And when Joseph's master heard the words of his wife, saying, "This is the way your servant treated me," his anger burned.
AMP.20: So Joseph's master took him and put him in the prison, a place where the king's prisoners were confined; so he was there in the prison.
AMP.21: But the LORD was with Joseph and extended lovingkindness to him, and gave him favor in the sight of the warden.
AMP.22: The warden committed to Joseph's care (management) all the prisoners who were in the prison; so that whatever was done there, he was in charge of it.
AMP.23: The warden paid no attention to anything that was in Joseph's care because the LORD was with him; whatever Joseph did, the LORD made to prosper.

NIV.1:
Joseph and Potiphar’s Wife
Now Joseph had been taken down to Egypt. Potiphar, an Egyptian who was one of Pharaoh’s officials, the captain of the guard, bought him from the Ishmaelites who had taken him there.
NIV.2: The Lord was with Joseph and he prospered, and he lived in the house of his Egyptian master.
NIV.3: When his master saw that the Lord was with him and that the Lord gave him success in everything he did,
NIV.4: Joseph found favor in his eyes and became his attendant. Potiphar put him in charge of his household, and he entrusted to his care everything he owned.
NIV.5: From the time he put him in charge of his household and of all that he owned, the Lord blessed the household of the Egyptian because of Joseph. The blessing of the Lord was on everything Potiphar had, both in the house and in the field.
NIV.6:
So he left in Joseph’s care everything he had; with Joseph in charge, he did not concern himself with anything except the food he ate.
Now Joseph was well-built and handsome,
NIV.7: and after a while his master’s wife took notice of Joseph and said, “Come to bed with me!”
NIV.8: But he refused. “With me in charge,” he told her, “my master does not concern himself with anything in the house; everything he owns he has entrusted to my care.
NIV.9: No one is greater in this house than I am. My master has withheld nothing from me except you, because you are his wife. How then could I do such a wicked thing and sin against God?”
NIV.10: And though she spoke to Joseph day after day, he refused to go to bed with her or even be with her.
NIV.11: One day he went into the house to attend to his duties, and none of the household servants was inside.
NIV.12: She caught him by his cloak and said, “Come to bed with me!” But he left his cloak in her hand and ran out of the house.
NIV.13: When she saw that he had left his cloak in her hand and had run out of the house,
NIV.14: she called her household servants. “Look,” she said to them, “this Hebrew has been brought to us to make sport of us! He came in here to sleep with me, but I screamed.
NIV.15: When he heard me scream for help, he left his cloak beside me and ran out of the house.”
NIV.16: She kept his cloak beside her until his master came home.
NIV.17: Then she told him this story: “That Hebrew slave you brought us came to me to make sport of me.
NIV.18: But as soon as I screamed for help, he left his cloak beside me and ran out of the house.”
NIV.19: When his master heard the story his wife told him, saying, “This is how your slave treated me,” he burned with anger.
NIV.20:
Joseph’s master took him and put him in prison, the place where the king’s prisoners were confined.
But while Joseph was there in the prison,
NIV.21: the Lord was with him; he showed him kindness and granted him favor in the eyes of the prison warden.
NIV.22: So the warden put Joseph in charge of all those held in the prison, and he was made responsible for all that was done there.
NIV.23: The warden paid no attention to anything under Joseph’s care, because the Lord was with Joseph and gave him success in whatever he did.
